problems.problem: The 'rind ring' is not readable as a concentric peel band: amber #f9a03f at opacity 0.45 over #e4691c shifts value by only a few percent, so in the poster the outer ring appears solely as two thin crescents poking out at the upper-left and upper-right of the ivory disc (approx x150-330/y500-760 and x750-930/y500-760). The declared 'outer peel scale ring offset behind the ivory slice' therefore reads as stray arcs rather than dial order, flattening the citrus-cross-section concept to a single disc.

Contact detail crop [268,1199,813,1440] confirms the shadow exists at base_y 1339 with offset_y 0 (correct contact, do not move down), but at opacity 0.3 / blur 10 / width_scale 0.92 it renders as a thin dark dash narrower than the 358px glass footprint, with two hard tick ends visible left and right of the base; on the flat silkscreen field the bottle reads slightly stickered rather than ink-grounded.

The register rule (decoration at y=396, height ~2px) sits in a dead zone: title block bottom is y=299 and cap top is y=446, leaving ~97px above and ~48px below the rule, so it floats untethered instead of 'padding under the title group' as in R1's locked nameplate; the quiet top band loses its monument-grid lock.

The declared nameplate specifies a wide-tracked light sans brand line ('wide-spaced Arial brand minimal at top'), but the logo 'Guerlain' is set in BOD_R.TTF serif; against the heavy two-line Bodoni title the brand line reads as a second serif voice, softening the brand-light/title-heavy contrast that R1's hierarchy relies on.
